title: Is Amazon.com (AMZN) Still Below Fair Value As AI Spending Rises?
detail:
Is Amazon.com (AMZN) Still Below Fair Value As AI Spending Rises?
Sasha Jovanovic
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 3:10 PM EST 4 min read
AMZN
Trade AMZN on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Amazon.com (AMZN) has moved to acquire Decart's AI optimization technology in a roughly US$7.5b deal, bringing its engineers in house to support Trainium chips and AWS-focused artificial intelligence workloads.

Against that backdrop, Amazon.com's share price has moved higher in recent months, with a year to date share price return of 12.75% and a 1 year total shareholder return of 12.86%. However, a softer 90 day share price return of a 2.17% decline suggests momentum has cooled slightly despite fresh AI deals and ongoing ETF trading swings around the stock.

Capitalize on the AI buildout around Amazon.com by scanning a curated set of 53 AI infrastructure stocks that could be next in line for attention.

Amazon.com keeps pouring cash into AI chips and data centers, even as free cash flow runs deeply negative. The business looks powerful. The open question is whether the current share price already reflects that strength.

Most Popular Narrative: 8.9% Undervalued

Against a last close of $255.39, the most followed narrative on Amazon.com pegs fair value at $280.21, using a 9% discount rate and focusing squarely on operating performance rather than headline net profit.

According to rcb9, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the narrative, the key is separating paper gains on AI stakes from the cash going into chips and data centers.

Handle the profit line carefully. Net income of $62.6 billion against $18.2 billion looks like a step change in the business. It is not. Non-operating pre-tax other income of $53.4 billion, primarily from the Anthropic stake, made up about two thirds of pre-tax income. That is paper appreciation on an equity position in a private company, not profit earned by selling goods, advertising or cloud capacity.

See why 43 investors see Amazon.com as 9% undervalued.

Result: Fair Value of $280.21 (UNDERVALUED)

Still, the narrative can crack if Amazon.com keeps posting negative free cash flow while capex climbs, or if AWS growth slows and backlog no longer supports the AI buildout.

Find out about the key risks to this Amazon.com narrative.

Another View: Amazon.com Through The P/E Lens

The cash flow narrative suggests Amazon.com is about 8.9% undervalued at $280.21 per share. A simple earnings multiple tells a different story. At a P/E of 20.5x, the stock appears slightly expensive versus the North American Multiline Retail industry on 19.9x and only modestly cheaper than peers on 21x.

The fair ratio points higher instead. Our estimate of a fair P/E near 38.4x implies the current 20.5x could still be conservative if the market shifts toward that benchmark. That gap may indicate potential upside if sentiment improves, or it may simply reflect the premium investors are already paying for Amazon.com.

Coatue Management's November 16 regulatory filing puts billionaire Philippe Laffont's positioning back in focus as investors look toward 2027. Its ten largest disclosed stock holdings represented 55.9% of a $54.5 billion reported portfolio at September 30, with chipmakers and equipment suppliers carrying much of the exposure.

In its May 6 public-markets update, Coatue highlighted the expanding token economy and identified AI agents as the industry's next major opportunity. That theme reaches beyond chip designers. Our look at AI holdings shared by two billionaire investors follows the spending into manufacturing equipment and electricity.

Those connections carry different risks. Infrastructure orders can support suppliers while construction bills pressure their customers' cash flow. A larger holding can also reflect price gains rather than fresh purchases. As with other high-conviction technology portfolios, the question for 2027 is whether growing demand will produce the earnings investors already expect.

Recently, we created a video looking at the 10 stocks billionaires Dalio and Laffont love. You can click below to see these stocks in our video on YouTube:

We covered the full selection in 10 High-Conviction Stocks Billionaire Philippe Laffont Is Betting On for 2027. Below, we look at the stocks ranked 10th through 6th.

Our Methodology

To compile our list, we reviewed Coatue Management's Q3 2026 13F filing and identified its ten largest stock holdings as of September 30, 2026, excluding ETFs and options. We used each holding's weight in the reported portfolio as a proxy for investment conviction and ranked the stocks from lowest to highest based on the value of Coatue's stake. We also included portfolio weights and changes in shares held from the previous quarter.

title: 3 Unstoppable Stocks That Can Be Great Buys for Decades
detail:
3 Unstoppable Stocks That Can Be Great Buys for Decades
David Jagielski, CPA, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 2:42 PM EST 5 min read
NVDA
AMZN
MSFT
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Stocks that are great long-term investments have solid underlying financials, and there's a great deal of predictability around their futures. What the recent Nvidia scandal has brought to light is the importance of investing in a business that may not be highly dependent on just a single person or the outlook for artificial intelligence (AI).

Three companies that look like unstoppable investments for the long term, regardless of what happens with AI, are Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT), and Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT). Here's why they can make for excellent buy-and-forget investments.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Amazon

Amazon's stock hasn't gotten much love over the past year. While it has generated decent 12% returns over the past 12 months, that pales in comparison to some of the gains tech stocks have accumulated over that stretch.

But for a company that's typically at the forefront of any tech innovation, its modest gains can actually be excellent news for investors who buy the stock today. While its financial results have been improving, its valuation hasn't taken off, and thus, it has become a much more attractive investment in the process.

The stock is currently trading at 23 times its expected future profits (based on analyst projections). That's a modest valuation for one of the leading tech companies in the world. It's developing robotaxis, its own AI chips, and deploying drones for delivery, among other opportunities it's pursuing. On top of all that is, of course, its massive e-commerce business.

To buy such a tremendous stock at a low valuation could prove to be a steal of a deal in the future.

Microsoft

Another tech giant that I like for the long haul is Microsoft. It's been a top name in tech for decades, and the reason I don't see that changing is because of how trusted and entrenched its software is within corporate environments. Businesses rely on Microsoft's Office software on a daily basis.

While there have been other options and there will continue to be more competition in the future, I think the reliability that its software offers and the trust it has built up over the years is what gives it a huge competitive advantage. And the company's investments in AI could also pay off significantly, with Microsoft's Office software now able to do much more, with its Copilot assistant helping create spreadsheets and documents in just minutes, potentially saving corporate clients hours each day.
